skill.name: lipsync
skill.description: Route lip-sync jobs to the right RunComfy model for source videos, portraits, or script-only workflows. The skill prepares documented runcomfy CLI invocations for Sync Labs, OmniHuman, Kling, Creatify, and related models.
skill.summary: Create lip-synced videos with RunComfy models and documented CLI commands.
skill.author: agentspace-so

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline model names, documentation links, and a token-storage disclosure. The main real risk is semantic: the skill enables lip-syncing faces to audio and leaves consent enforcement to the operator.

remediation.issue: Dual-use synthetic media depends on operator-only consent checks.
remediation.suggestion: Add a mandatory pre-run consent checklist for the face subject, voice owner, source footage, and intended use.

remediation.issue: External media processing sends user assets to RunComfy services.
remediation.suggestion: Require users to acknowledge that media URLs and generated outputs leave the local environment before running jobs.

remediation.issue: Shell examples depend on CLI installation and credentials.
remediation.suggestion: Keep bash scope limited to runcomfy commands and avoid adding remote install scripts or arbitrary shell pipelines.

semantic_findings.title: Dual-use Face and Voice Impersonation Risk
semantic_findings.description: The skill is designed to drive a face mouth from a separate audio track and states that it does not gate inputs. This can support nonconsensual impersonation unless operators enforce consent checks.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The skill text explicitly describes real-person consent requirements and leaves enforcement to the operator. That confirms a real semantic misuse risk, even though the file includes mitigation guidance.

content.value_statement: Lip sync work often requires choosing the right model for each input type. This skill routes video, portrait, or script workflows to RunComfy commands.
actual_capabilities: Selects Sync Labs sync v2 or Pro for lip sync on existing videos.
Selects OmniHuman for portrait-and-audio talking avatar jobs.
Selects Kling or HappyHorse options when the user has a script but no audio file.
Provides runcomfy CLI commands with model names, input fields, and output directory guidance.
Explains audio quality, duration matching, and route selection tradeoffs.
Includes consent, endpoint, token storage, and shell-scope guidance.
limitations: Requires the RunComfy CLI, account access, and valid API credentials.
Requires media files or URLs that the selected RunComfy model can access.
Does not verify legal consent or ownership of faces, voices, or source videos.
Generated quality depends on the chosen model, source footage, and clean audio.

use_cases.title: Localize a Brand Video
use_cases.description: Choose Sync Labs Pro for a translated voiceover on an existing product video.

use_cases.title: Create a Presenter Avatar
use_cases.description: Use OmniHuman with a portrait and voiceover to make a talking-head video.

use_cases.title: Prototype Scripted Social Clips
use_cases.description: Route a script-only idea to Kling or HappyHorse for generated speech and synced video.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Lip Sync Route
prompt_templates.prompt: I have an existing video and a clean voiceover file. Choose the best RunComfy lip sync route and explain why.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Portrait Avatar Job
prompt_templates.prompt: Use a portrait image and voiceover to prepare an OmniHuman RunComfy job. Include the required inputs and key quality checks.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Multi-Language Dub
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a multi-language lip sync workflow for one approved presenter video and several translated audio tracks.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Advanced Model Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare Sync Labs Pro, Sync Labs v2, Kling lipsync, and OmniHuman for this project. Recommend one route with risk and cost notes.

output_examples.input: Existing spokesperson video with a Spanish voiceover file.
output_examples.output: Recommendation to use Sync Labs Pro, with notes about audio cleanup, duration matching, and the RunComfy job shape.

output_examples.input: Single portrait image and a product pitch audio track.
output_examples.output: Recommendation to use OmniHuman, with framing guidance and consent checks for the face and voice.

output_examples.input: Short script for a social clip, with no recorded audio.
output_examples.output: Recommendation to use a script-to-video route, with a warning that generated speech will not match a fixed MP3.

best_practices: Confirm consent for every face and voice before running a lip sync job.
Use clean speech audio and match the audio length to the source video.
Start with the highest-fidelity route for final delivery and cheaper routes for drafts.
anti_patterns: Do not target real people, public figures, or private individuals without explicit consent.
Do not use noisy music-heavy audio when accurate mouth movement matters.
Do not treat script-generated audio routes as replacements for a fixed voiceover file.

faq.question: What does this skill use RunComfy for?
faq.answer: It prepares model-specific RunComfy CLI commands for lip sync and talking-avatar workflows.

faq.question: Can it work with an existing video?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends Sync Labs or Kling audio-to-video routes for existing video plus audio.

faq.question: Can it create a video from only a portrait and audio?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends OmniHuman for portrait-and-audio avatar-style output.

faq.question: Can it generate speech from a script?
faq.answer: Yes. It can route script-only requests to models that generate speech during video creation.

faq.question: Does it verify consent automatically?
faq.answer: No. The operator must verify rights for the face, voice, source footage, and intended use.

faq.question: What tools are required?
faq.answer: You need the RunComfy CLI, a RunComfy account, valid credentials, and accessible input media.
